rationale: Requires data passed between stages to arrive without modification, which is integrity.
Signature validation confirms the message origin is a registered airline (authenticity) and a signature also detects alteration (integrity).
Encrypting radar records so unauthorised readers cannot interpret them protects confidentiality.
Restricts who may modify bookmarks and entries to the profile owner whose identity is verified in the session.
Admits a customer only after identifier and credential are validated, which is authentication.
Verifies claimed identity through certificate validation at login.
Verifies supplied credentials against registered users before granting access, which is authentication.
A cryptographic signature is attached so later changes to the amount can be detected, which is integrity.
Credential reset for a registered developer via a link to the email on file is an identity-verification and credential recovery mechanism, weakly authenticity.
Proprietary parameters must arrive encrypted and are rejected otherwise, protecting them from disclosure.
Checksum verification refuses use of modified components, protecting program integrity; no attack is named explicitly.
Protects encryption keys from being read by other applications, preserving confidentiality of recordings.
Reacts to a re-sent (replayed) licence grant by aborting, which is replay handling.
A hash on the balance detects alteration and the purse refuses to operate on mismatch, which is integrity.
Validates the accuracy and consistency of recording metadata and rejects duplicate identifiers, which is data validity and integrity.
Transmitting only over encrypted connections so intermediaries cannot read values is confidentiality.
Hash comparison blocks payment if the approved batch was altered, which is integrity.
Per-module grants of who may view and who may alter content cover both read and modify access control.
Detects and blocks script injection while keeping simulations running, which is resisting attack.
Removes user names, paths and snippets from crash reports so support staff cannot see them, protecting privacy.
Guarantees consistent amounts across transfer legs and rejects mismatches, which is data coherence and integrity.
Purges intermediate datasets so later users cannot read them, preventing disclosure.
Dashboard access is conditional on the controller confirming the resident identity.
Recomputing the ledger checksum and retaining the rolled-back entry unchanged preserves data integrity.
Public-key encryption conceals session keys during distribution, protecting confidentiality.
Rejects and reports crafted inputs meant to exhaust the training service, which is resisting abuse.
Requires proof of profile ownership through a verified credential before restoring data, which is authentication.
Validates entry accuracy (integrity) and detects and rejects injected or manipulated entries that bypass checks (resistance).
Requires the cardholder to enter the correct PIN, which is authentication.
Responds to an attacker replay of an authentication assertion by terminating the session and clearing state.
Verifying a keyed authentication tag on each command checks alteration and the paired hub as origin.
Requires sign-in with an enrolled account and valid credential before launch, which is authentication.
Discards stale commands so recorded commands cannot be replayed to operate a lock, which is replay resistance.
Informs whether a dataset has a verifiable stamp confirming the provider identity, which concerns origin authenticity.
Erases personal and payment data from temporary storage on timeout to prevent exposure.
Digest comparison detects a modified source file before compilation, which is integrity.

Prevents partial updates and restricts modification to users with an edit role, both integrity.
